signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Tension
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades under pressure as JPY leads the G10 scorecard with a +1.201% average gain, while CHF lags at -1.012%. The leader-to-laggard spread of 2.213% signals a major structural divergence, amplified by escalating US-Iran tensions which traditionally favor JPY over CHF in Asian energy-security contexts. JPY COT LF net short remains extreme at -124,575, but a strong positive ESI of +22.9 and a 1.20% weekly average gain suggest a crowded short-covering cycle is underway. Despite a -100bp carry disadvantage for JPY (SNB 0.0% vs BoJ 1.0%), the JPY safe-haven bid is dominating as cross-asset correlations shift. Risk: Crude oil prices stabilize and Middle East tensions de-escalate, allowing carry-seeking flows to return to CHF crosses.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options + Volatility
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.503, holding just above its SMA200 at 158.05 after failing to sustain levels above the SMA20/50 cluster near 161.43. The options market is aggressively pricing downside protection, with the 25d RR at -2.30 marking a strong put skew that contradicts the +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%). Notably, USD/JPY IV at 7.2% sits below realized HV30 at 8.5%, creating a -1.3% vol risk premium that signals unusual complacency despite significant downside technical risks. While household spending misses weaken the BoJ's hike path, the crowded COT spec short at -124,575 remains vulnerable to further liquidations if the 158.05 level fails. Risk: A sustained close below SMA200 at 158.05 triggers a disorderly unwind of the carry trade toward 155.00.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs ESI Divergence + RBNZ
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5866 remains positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5791-0.5829), supported by a top-tier ESI of +24.4 following a string of data beats. COT LF net positioning is extremely short at -30,606 (long% 9.7%), creating a sharp divergence between bearish speculative positioning and improving domestic fundamentals. While the RBNZ is in a hiking cycle (2.5%), the pair faces a +125bp carry deficit against the Fed (3.75%), which has kept specs sidelined. Retail sentiment is also 70% short, aligning with institutional shorts and increasing the risk of a combined short-squeeze if the Sep 2 RBNZ meeting delivers a hawkish surprise. Risk: RBNZ pauses hiking cycle, validating the deep spec short and breaking the SMA support cluster.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Volatility + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7030, holding above its SMA20/50 cluster at 0.7000 ahead of the Aug 11 RBA meeting. Options markets are pricing extreme uncertainty with an +8.5% Vol Risk Premium (IV 14.7% vs HV30 6.2%), indicating high demand for tail-risk hedging. Retail sentiment has moved to a 73% short bias, diverging from the COT LF net long of +23,616, suggesting retail traders are fading the recent move into a restrictive real rate environment (+0.60%). This institutional vs. retail divergence at a key technical juncture typically precedes a trend extension rather than a reversal. Risk: RBA adopts a dovish tone on Tuesday, triggering retail profit-taking and institutional liquidations.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Yield Differential + Volatility
signals.text: EUR/USD at 1.1523 remains confined below its SMA200 of 1.1633, weighed down by a +135bp nominal carry disadvantage (Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.4%). ECB holds at 2.4%. Volatility pricing shows an elevated premium with IV at 7.1% vs HV30 at 4.4%, suggesting the market is paying for protection against a break of the current range rather than expecting realized vol to stay low. Speculative positioning is net short -92,930, but the lack of a strong 25d RR skew (-0.34) suggests no immediate conviction for a breakdown. Risk: ECB shifts to a 'hold' bias in September, widening the real rate gap and forcing a test of the 1.1450 SMA20 support.
